# sites per 1,000 residents, with an exact Poisson 95% interval
ranked = areas %>%
  filter(pop >= 1) %>%
  mutate(rate  = sites / pop * 1000,
         lower = qchisq(0.025, 2 * sites) / 2 / pop * 1000,
         upper = qchisq(0.975, 2 * (sites + 1)) / 2 / pop * 1000)

# funnel plot: the city rate and its 95% / 99.8% control limits at each population
m = sum(ranked$sites) / sum(ranked$pop)
ranked = ranked %>%
  mutate(hi95 = (m + 1.96 * sqrt(m / pop)) * 1000,
         hi998 = (m + 3.09 * sqrt(m / pop)) * 1000)

leader = ranked$cell[which.max(ranked$rate)]
ranked = ranked %>%
  arrange(desc(rate))
top10 = ranked %>%
  arrange(desc(rate)) %>%
  head(10)

ranked %>%
  summarize(n_areas = n(), city_rate = m * 1000,
            top_cell = first(cell), top_value = first(rate), top_pop = first(pop),
            leader_rank = which(cell == leader),
            leader_lower = lower[cell == leader], leader_upper = upper[cell == leader],
            n_above_998 = sum(rate > hi998))

# sites per 1,000 residents, with an exact Poisson 95% interval
ranked = areas %>%
  filter(pop >= 1) %>%
  mutate(rate  = sites / pop * 1000,
         lower = qchisq(0.025, 2 * sites) / 2 / pop * 1000,
         upper = qchisq(0.975, 2 * (sites + 1)) / 2 / pop * 1000)

# funnel plot: the city rate and its 95% / 99.8% control limits at each population
m = sum(ranked$sites) / sum(ranked$pop)
ranked = ranked %>%
  mutate(hi95 = (m + 1.96 * sqrt(m / pop)) * 1000,
         hi998 = (m + 3.09 * sqrt(m / pop)) * 1000)

# empirical Bayes: pull each rate toward m, harder when pop is small
r = ranked$sites / ranked$pop
s2 = sum(ranked$pop * (r - m)^2) / sum(ranked$pop)
A = max(s2 - m / mean(ranked$pop), 0)
ranked = ranked %>%
  mutate(weight = A / (A + m / pop),
         shrunk = (m + weight * (sites / pop - m)) * 1000)

leader = ranked$cell[which.max(ranked$rate)]
ranked = ranked %>%
  arrange(desc(shrunk))
top10 = ranked %>%
  arrange(desc(shrunk)) %>%
  head(10)

ranked %>%
  summarize(n_areas = n(), city_rate = m * 1000,
            top_cell = first(cell), top_value = first(shrunk), top_pop = first(pop),
            leader_rank = which(cell == leader),
            leader_lower = lower[cell == leader], leader_upper = upper[cell == leader],
            n_above_998 = sum(rate > hi998))
